studies.finding: The source identifies N-termini for 132 chromatophore-encoded and 76 nucleus-encoded proteins. Of 37 nuclear proteins carrying the source transit-peptide annotation, thirty show processing in a common region; most retain the second transit-peptide part.
limitations: The current measurements depend on older protein models/transcript data and one publication; culture triplicates are not independent laboratories.
Isolation largely loses the outer membrane and can leave contamination or surface-associated proteins. Long nuclear proteins lacking clear transit peptides are not all certified as imported.

The source identified 208 proteins in this N-terminome, not the whole organelle proteome or universal protein-import requirements. LC-MS detectability and possible degradation affect processing interpretation.

No in-vitro import assay, AP-1 binding measurement, membrane-fusion imaging, genetic reconstruction or proteomics replay was performed here. Historical engulfment and modern targeting have distinct evidential status.
